commentary: The ranking exhibits clear stratification across global venues. Nasdaq 100 and NYSE dominate as tier-one leaders, with Nasdaq 100 posting the tightest ILLIQ at 0.0025% per $1M traded and NYSE delivering the lowest AR spread at 0.6259%, though NYSE trails in comparable volume at $208.4M versus Nasdaq 100's $324.0M. The mid-tier comprises Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, and SIX Swiss Exchange, where Tokyo distinguishes itself with robust 2.9448% turnover ratio and $48.3M comparable volume despite a higher 0.0370% per $1M ILLIQ cost. Notably, Euronext presents a metric divergence—its 0.5580% AR spread ranks best among mid-tier venues, yet its ILLIQ of 0.0304% per $1M remains elevated relative to that spread tightness, suggesting latency or inventory effects. Hong Kong Stock Exchange, Xetra, and London Stock Exchange form a secondary tier with moderate spreads but constrained volumes under $10M. Korea Exchange ranks last, with both the worst ILLIQ at 0.1516% per $1M and an outlier AR spread of 1.5745%, reflecting structural liquidity fragmentation despite modest $15.0M turnover.
